oud-perfume-guide.before:
Oud is one of the most talked-about notes in perfume: deep, woody and a little smoky. Designer houses such as Tom Ford, Gucci, Guerlain and Chopard each have their own take on it. Here is what oud is, how the best-known oud perfumes differ, and how to choose and wear one.

What is oud?

Oud, also called agarwood or aoud, is a dark, fragrant resin that forms in the wood of agar (Aquilaria) trees. It has been treasured in the Middle East and South Asia for centuries, burned as incense and worn as an oil. Natural oud is rare, so many modern perfumes use an oud accord: a blend of woods, resins and leathery notes built to give the same rich effect. Gucci, for example, lists an oud accord in its base notes.

Tom Ford Oud Wood

Tom Ford Oud Wood Eau de Parfum (from £115.99, 30ml or 50ml) is the gentlest way into oud. Its key notes are oud wood, rosewood and cardamom over sandalwood, vetiver, tonka bean and amber, so the oud reads smooth and warm rather than smoky. It is unisex and easy to wear in the office or in the evening. See every Tom Ford fragrance.

Gucci Intense Oud

Gucci Intense Oud Eau de Parfum (£73.99, 90ml) is darker. Black pepper and olibanum (frankincense) open it; amber woods, sandalwood and cedarwood sit at the heart; leather, patchouli, gurjun balsam and the oud accord form the base. Expect incense and leather more than sweetness. Shop all Gucci.

Tom Ford Oud Wood or Gucci Intense Oud?

  • Choose Oud Wood if you want a soft, creamy wood with a touch of spice that suits everyday wear.
  • Choose Intense Oud if you like incense, leather and a bolder, smokier trail for evenings and colder months.

Three more oud perfumes

  • Guerlain Oud Essentiel (£94.99, 125ml): saffron and pelargonium, then rose, oud and cedarwood over leather, frankincense and guaiac wood. A rose-and-leather oud, made unisex.
  • Chopard Oud Malaki (£48.99, 80ml): grapefruit, lavender and artemisia, then tobacco, spices and leather over oud, ambergris and dark woods. Made for men, and the most affordable oud in this guide.
  • Montale Aoud Damascus (£52.99, 100ml): damask rose, aoud and saffron with amber, woods and musk. Montale is known for rose and oud, and this one is made for women.

The Al Haramain Amber Oud editions

Al Haramain's Amber Oud range is a popular Arabian line, but read the notes: not every edition is built around oud. Amber Oud White Edition (from £34.99) is bergamot and orange, then jasmine, rose and freesia over musk, vanilla and patchouli, and is listed for women. Amber Oud Carbon Edition (from £35.99) is a fresh, aromatic men's scent of lavender, rosemary, bergamot, sage and vetiver. Amber Oud Bleu Edition (from £38.99) is citrus and mint over incense, vetiver and sandalwood. For the Gold, Ruby, Tobacco and Black editions, and for Lattafa, read our guide to Arabian perfume and Lattafa Khamrah Qahwa.

Which oud perfume suits you?

  • New to oud: Tom Ford Oud Wood, or a fresher Amber Oud edition.
  • You love incense and leather: Gucci Intense Oud or Guerlain Oud Essentiel.
  • You love rose: Montale Aoud Damascus or Guerlain Oud Essentiel.
  • Warm and spicy: Chopard Oud Malaki.

Oud is traditionally unisex, so "for men" or "for women" on the label is only a starting point. Browse unisex perfume, perfume for men and perfume for women.

How to wear oud

  1. Start small: one or two sprays. Oud notes are rich, and a little goes a long way.
  2. Apply to moisturised skin on the wrists, neck or chest. Our guide to layering oud with body butter explains why.
  3. Let it settle: do not rub your wrists together. Oud perfumes often change a lot after the first half hour, so judge them later in the day.
  4. Test before you buy a full bottle if you can, or start with a smaller size.

Good to know

  • Eau de parfum is the most common strength for oud perfumes; read extrait vs eau de parfum for what the label means.
  • Patch test on your inner arm if you have sensitive skin, and keep perfume away from your eyes.
  • Store bottles away from heat and sunlight, with the cap on.

moisturiser-for-your-skin-type.before:
A good moisturiser is the step that holds the rest of your routine together. It softens skin, helps it feel comfortable all day and gives make-up or sunscreen a smooth base. But the right texture depends on your skin: a rich cream that rescues dry skin can feel heavy on oily skin, and a light lotion may not be enough in winter. Here is how to choose a moisturiser for your skin type.

Cream, lotion or gel: what is the difference?

Most moisturisers mix water with oils and butters. The more oil and butter, the richer the texture:

  • Rich creams hold more butters and oils, such as shea butter and almond oil. They suit dry and very dry skin, and cold weather.
  • Light creams and lotions have more water and lighter oils. They suit normal, oily and combination skin.
  • Gels and serums are mostly water with moisture-loving ingredients such as glycerine and hyaluronic acid. They work on their own for oily skin, or under a cream.

Moisturiser for dry skin

Dry skin feels tight, may flake and drinks a light lotion straight in. Look for a cream with butters and oils.

Deyga Deep Moisturising Face Cream (£18.99, 30g) blends shea butter with marula and almond oils, centella asiatica (gotu kola) and cardamom, and Deyga makes it without artificial fragrance. Highborn London Imperial Moisturiser (£46, 50ml) is a richer, nourishing cream made in England for dry, tight-feeling skin. See more moisturisers for dry skin.

Moisturiser for oily skin

Oily skin still needs moisture: skipping it can leave skin feeling tight while it still looks shiny. Choose a light, fast-absorbing texture.

Deyga Light Moisturising Face Cream (£18.99, 30g) is made for oily and normal skin, with rosehip, almond and avocado oils, shea butter, centella asiatica and ectoin, and a hint of vanilla essential oil. On very oily days, a serum such as Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (£22.99, 20ml) can be enough on its own. More ideas for oily skin.

Moisturiser for sensitive skin

Sensitive skin does best with a short ingredient list and no added fragrance. Of the creams above, the Deyga Deep Moisturising Face Cream is made without artificial fragrance; the Light cream contains vanilla essential oil, so patch test it first. Introduce one new product at a time, and see more for sensitive skin.

Moisturiser for combination skin

Combination skin is oily through the centre and normal or dry on the cheeks. Use a light moisturiser all over and add a little richer cream only where skin feels dry. Vilvah Ultra Moisturising Cream (£25.99, 50ml) is a good middle ground: olive squalane, glycerine and plant extracts in a non-greasy cream that Vilvah makes for all skin types, with white lily essential oil.

Add a hydrating serum underneath

Serums are light and watery, so they go on before your moisturiser. A hyaluronic acid serum such as the Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (sodium hyaluronate, panthenol, aloe and centella) or Vilvah Milk Drops Hydrating Serum (from £21.99), with aloe vera juice, hyaluronic acid and rice milk extract, adds a layer of moisture that the cream then seals in. Aloe vera gel works in a similar way; read how to use aloe vera gel. Browse every serum.

Day cream or night cream?

By day, your moisturiser sits under sunscreen and make-up, so a lighter texture often works best. Finish with SPF, or use a moisturiser with SPF built in, such as Highborn London GLOWGUARD SPF30 Moisturiser (from £49), which uses non-nano zinc oxide.

At night there is no sunscreen or make-up to layer, so many people like something richer. A night cream such as Highborn London Night Elixir (from £26) is a comforting cream made for the last step of an evening routine. The Ultimate Day & Night Moisture Set (£95) pairs it with the Imperial Moisturiser.

How to apply moisturiser

  1. Cleanse with a face wash that suits your skin: see face wash for your skin type.
  2. Apply serum, if you use one, to slightly damp skin.
  3. Warm a pea-sized amount of moisturiser between your fingertips.
  4. Press and smooth it over your face and neck with upward strokes, avoiding the eyes. For the eye area, see our under eye cream guide.
  5. In the morning, finish with sunscreen unless your moisturiser has SPF.

What makes a moisturiser "natural"?

There is no legal definition of "natural" in the UK, so read the ingredient list rather than the label. In the creams above you will find plant butters and oils (shea, marula, rosehip, avocado, almond, olive squalane) alongside glycerine, water and an emulsifier that keeps them blended. Full ingredient lists are on every product page.

Good to know

  • Patch test a new moisturiser on your jaw or inner arm for 24 hours.
  • Your skin changes with the seasons: many people switch to a richer cream in winter and a lighter one in summer.
  • Dryness, redness or itching that lasts is worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

under-eye-cream-guide.before:
The skin around your eyes is thinner than the rest of your face, and it moves every time you blink, smile or squint. That is why many people give it its own product. An under eye cream is a small, gentle moisturiser made for this delicate area. Here is how to choose one, how to apply it, and what to expect.

Do you need an eye cream?

You can use your face moisturiser around the eyes, as long as it does not sting. An eye cream is worth it if your moisturiser feels too rich or makes your eyes water, if the area feels dry or tight, or if you simply enjoy a separate step. Eye creams come in small jars, have a texture made for patting on, and are usually made without added fragrance.

Cream, gel or balm?

  • Light creams suit most skin and sit well under make-up.
  • Gels feel cool and weightless, and suit oily skin or a morning routine.
  • Balms and oils are richer, and suit dry skin or a night routine.

Under eye creams to try

Deyga Under Eye Cream (from £14.99, 15g) is a light, cooling cream of aloe vera, cucumber hydrosol, almond oil, potato starch and vitamin E. Deyga makes it without silicones, parabens or artificial fragrance, and it can sit under make-up. Vilvah Natural Under Eye Cream (£19.99, 20ml) is a little richer: glycerine, witch hazel, shea butter and sunflower seed oil with bamboo, goji berry and cardamom extracts, made without alcohol or silicones.
